$comment: TIER MANIFEST for .claude/agents/*.md — the source of truth for BOTH the preferred
(rubric) model+effort of every agent and the degraded-capacity fallback.
Copy this file to .claude/agent-model-tiers.json and give EVERY agent file an entry.
agent-model-tier.py refuses to run until the manifest and .claude/agents/ agree in
both directions — an agent with no entry, or an entry with no file, is an error, not
a skip.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. It records every agent's model + effort in one reviewed place,
and `agent-model-tier.py check` goes red the moment a file and the manifest disagree.
If you change an agent's tier by hand, change it here in the same commit.
DEFAULTS. Every agent runs `opus` (an ALIAS, never a dated id) with an EXPLICIT effort.
An omitted effort inherits the launching session, whose default is the MODEL's default
-- `medium` on Opus 5.5 (code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config) -- so no entry uses null.
`high` for document-shaped work; `xhigh` where the deliverable is a decision, diagnosis
or gate verdict (the review gate and test runner among them); `max` only on a measured gain.
THE FALLBACK COLUMN SHIPS IDENTICAL TO `preferred`, so `apply fallback` changes nothing
until you configure it. If your plan has a per-model quota, you MAY record a cheaper
model per agent here as a capacity escape. Then the flip is mechanical but the RESTORE
is not: an LLM re-deriving 'which agents go back' later produces a plausible roster
with no error anywhere, so the restore reads from THIS FILE, never from re-derivation.
AUTHORITY. skills/_shared/review-checklist.md 'Model + effort rubric' stays
authoritative for `preferred`. This file RECORDS that rubric's output plus a fallback
column; it does not override it. A rubric change means editing both, same commit.
THE FALLBACK IS NOT A RE-TIERING. `preferred` is untouched by a fallback and is what
the roster returns to. Do not cite `mode: fallback` as evidence the rubric changed.
USAGE: agent-model-tier.py {status|check|apply preferred|apply fallback} [--tier N] [--dry-run]
mode_set_by: <WHO DECIDED, AND HOW — e.g. 'founder, quota alert'>
mode_reason: <WHY THE CURRENT MODE IS IN EFFECT — for `preferred`: 'normal operation'>
restore_when: <THE CONDITION THAT ENDS A FALLBACK — e.g. 'weekly quota resets, or enough frees up to restore tier 1'. Partial budget: restore by ascending restore_tier (`apply preferred --tier N`), verifying each step with `check --mode preferred --tier N`.>

fallback_effort_policy.rule: PRESERVE the preferred effort on the fallback model unless a reviewed exception below says otherwise. Nothing else moves.
fallback_effort_policy.why_preserve_is_the_default: Without a measurement that a higher effort on the fallback model beats the preferred effort, the standing discipline is 'start high, raise only on measured gain'. Blanket-promoting agents burns the fallback model's headroom on a hunch.

exceptions.$comment: Empty until you configure a fallback model. Record any agent whose effort you deliberately change on the fallback, and why -- e.g. an effort held down on the preferred model only because of a mechanism specific to that model.

fallback_effort_policy.reviewed_and_left_alone: <LIST OR DESCRIBE the agents you reviewed and deliberately kept at their preferred effort, so the next reader knows it was a decision, not an omission.>

restore_tiers.1: Irreversible or fleet-wide blast radius: orchestration, the review gate, money/auth, schema, prod-state mutation, any production kill-switch. Restore these first on any partial budget.
restore_tiers.2: Cross-system diagnosis and user-facing content authoring. A wrong root cause sends real work down the wrong path; wrong content ships to users, but offline and reviewable.
restore_tiers.3: Product-domain and long-prose specialists. Prose quality degrades least on the fallback model; restore last.

excluded.$comment: Files that carry a model pin OUTSIDE .claude/agents/ (a worker compose file, a CLI wrapper) and must NOT be flipped by a fallback sweep. Key = path, value = why. Empty until you have one.
